Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 5) demonstrates a markedly enlarged cardiac silhouette with a distinct translucent line outlining the mediastinal border (indicated by arrows), which represents the "varying cardiac density sign" or pericardial fat pad sign indicative of a large pericardial effusion such as haemopericardium. This radiographic appearance distinguishes it from simple cardiomegaly or normal contours.
